narrative.overview:
My Living Drawing is a quiet animator's workbench: warm drafting paper supports a translucent tracing-paper stage, graphite defines structure, blue-pencil guides reveal construction, and restrained colored-pencil fills make characters and props feel touched by hand. The interface resembles a working animation lightbox rather than a polished AI dashboard or bright game template.

Identity survives from character choice to motion through low-saturation authored sprites and hand-drawn CSS scenery. Scene objects are native-button pieces with bounded pointer and touch dragging, grab/grabbing feedback, a blue-pencil dashed drag frame, and a synchronized range-control alternative in the scene editor.
keyCharacteristics: Drafting paper, tracing paper, graphite structure, blue-pencil guides, and low-saturation colored-pencil fills form one unmistakable world.
One framed stage is the interaction anchor; supporting controls stay compact and tactile.
AI-authored character identities remain recognizable across dedicated motion frames.
CSS scenery and hand-drawn props use graphite construction and subdued fill rather than glossy clip art.
All quick actions use one graphite inline-SVG stroke family.
Motion is short, readable, object-specific, and fully reduced when requested.
The living world and its white paper conversation card read as one responsive two-column play surface.
Conversation stays continuous through pale tracing-paper assistant bubbles, muted red-pencil user bubbles, typing dots, quick topics, and one composer.
The world header uses normal-sized, novice-friendly plain-text tools; concise verbs explain the result without oversized or infantilized controls.
A 60-item, seven-category material library and a 120-preset house decoration studio extend the paper world with code-native hand-drawn previews.
Direct scene manipulation supports mouse, pen, and touch while measured bounds keep complete objects inside the stage.
The scene editor exposes the same coordinates and bounds through labeled range controls for keyboard users.
Compact mobile treatment begins at `560px` with two-row navigation, `44px` controls, contained horizontal rails, and zero page overflow down to `320px`.

rules.name: The One Red-Pencil Voice Rule
rules.body: Colored-pencil red signals action or deliberate emphasis; never scatter it as general decoration.

rules.name: The Graphite Structure Rule
rules.body: Interactive shapes, authored props, and action icons share graphite definition over layered paper.

rules.name: The Blue Pencil Rule
rules.body: Blue pencil explains construction, position, and movement without competing with action red.

rules.name: The Friendly Weight Rule
rules.body: Use strong weight, compact line length, and scale for hierarchy; do not introduce thin editorial typography.

rules.name: The Plain-Language Tool Rule
rules.body: Header utilities stay at normal control scale and use short concrete verbs. Child-friendly means immediately understandable, not oversized, babyish, or visually loud.

rules.name: The One Stage Rule
rules.body: Each step has one dominant framed task surface; secondary controls orbit it instead of creating competing dashboards.

rules.name: The Layered Paper Rule
rules.body: Use thin graphite borders and warm ambient shadows for sheet order; reserve stronger lift for active dragging.

dos: Do keep drafting paper, tracing paper, graphite, blue-pencil guides, and subdued colored-pencil fills consistent across every surface.
Do preserve each AI companion's identity across its dedicated motion frames.
Do author scene props as simple hand-drawn CSS forms with graphite edges and restrained warm shadows.
Do use the same graphite inline-SVG stroke style for every quick action.
Do keep the joint overlay optional, labeled by anatomy, and visually secondary during motion.
Do keep chat as one continuous transcript with pale tracing-paper assistant bubbles, muted red-pencil user bubbles, visible typing feedback, and action-linked replies.
Do preserve speaker attribution when switching between two companions in one transcript.
Do keep scene dragging bounded, touch-capable, and visible through grab/grabbing, temporary lift, and a blue-pencil dashed frame.
Do keep labeled scene-editor ranges synchronized as the keyboard-accessible alternative to direct dragging.
Do keep story tasks progressive and subordinate to the scene they control.
Do reuse the shared graphite scrim and warm-paper shell for export, safety, and rest reminders; use a directional drawer for scene editing.
Do preserve the `1050px`, `820px`, and `560px` responsive behaviors, two-row mobile navigation, `44px` controls, zero horizontal overflow, shared gold focus ring, and reduced-motion override.
Do keep Chinese copy concise, warm, honest about local Demo behavior, and immediately actionable.
Do use normal-sized plain-text header tools and concrete child-facing verbs: `加东西`, `装房子`, `移动东西`, `放前面`, `放后面`, and `拿走`.
Do keep all 60 library items and 120 house presets visually previewable with code-native hand-drawn forms before selection.
Do give every modal initial focus, `Escape` dismissal, contained tab order, and focus restoration to its launcher.
donts: Don't turn the experience into a generic AI upload dashboard or dense control console.
Don't replace a selected character with a generic DOM puppet or unrelated animation asset.
Don't use emoji as the primary living-world art for sun, tree, apple, house, or dog when authored assets and CSS props exist.
Don't mix icon libraries, filled glyphs, or emoji into the unified quick-action SVG family.
Don't add gradients as ornamental UI styling, glass effects, or low-contrast decoration; the stage's day/night sky transition is functional scenery.
Don't show joint nodes permanently or force animal anatomy into human shoulder-and-hip terminology.
Don't fragment the conversation into a stack of heavy cards or detach it visually and behaviorally from the living world.
Don't reset the transcript when switching companions or duplicate the chat surface.
Don't stack story, editor, export, or safety layers into a competing control dashboard.
Don't compress mobile utility controls below the touch-safe envelope to force one-line navigation.
Don't let any object cross the measured stage boundary or let drag completion fire its click action.
Don't make drag the only positioning method or allow horizontal rails to widen the page.
Don't imply live AI capability or saved personal data when the shipped experience is local and replaceable.
Don't use “图层” in child-facing UI or substitute oversized, infantilized controls for clear novice-friendly wording.
Don't render material choices as generic chips or house presets as partial color swatches; show the whole object being chosen.
